HP:0004991.label: Rhizomelic arm shortening
HP:0004991.text: mild rhizomelic shortness of upper limbs

records.label: Brother with ante-mortem labs and autopsy

phenotypes.text: mild rhizomelic shortness of upper limbs

quotes: Both died at three days of cardio-respiratory insufficiency, but only one had ante-mortem lab tests which showed low calcium, high phosphorus, and high alkaline phosphatase levels attributed to a renal defect.
On autopsy this same infant was found to have pulmonary, renal and adrenal hemorrhage, and subendocardial myocarditis and myocardial necrosis.

records.label: Second brother

phenotypes.text: mild rhizomelic shortness of upper limbs

quotes: This is a report of two brothers, born within a year of each other, with a similar skeletal disorder of severe congenital metaphyseal involvement, mild rhizomelic shortness of upper limbs, and mild platyspondyly.
Both died at three days of cardio-respiratory insufficiency

records.label: Affected baby girl (sib)
quotes: since parents are normal and recently had an affected baby girl, it is presumed that this disorder is an autosomal recessive trait.

records.label: Iranian infant (second Iranian family)
quotes: Here data are presented on another Iranian infant with the Sedaghatian syndrome who died on day 4 and was found to have histologic evidence of severe epimetaphyseal dysplasia.

records.label: Reported infant
quotes: We report our findings of another infant with a lethal course.

records.label: Two unrelated cases
quotes: We present the radiological findings in two unrelated cases with spondylometaphyseal dysplasia type Sedaghatian.

records.label: Infant born to Yemeni parents

phenotypes.text: radiologic findings of lethal metaphyseal chondrodysplasia

quotes: We report a case of spondylometaphyseal dysplasia in an infant who was born to nonconsanguineous Yemeni parents. Radiological findings were consistent with lethal metaphyseal chondrodysplasia (Sedaghatian type).
Although all previously reported cases died within 4 days of life, our patient survived 161 days.

records.label: Female infant
quotes: This child, born to nonconsanguineous Caucasian parents, was hypotonic from birth and experienced recurrent cyanotic episodes within a few hours of delivery.
Cerebral imaging revealed absence of the corpus callosum and marked frontotemporal pachygyria. She developed seizures on day 14 of life and died at the age of 17 days.

records.label: Patient
quotes: We report on a patient with Sedaghatian type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia (SSMD) who presented with metaphyseal dysplasia, congenital atrioventricular block, simplified gyral pattern, hypogenesis of corpus callosum, and severe cerebellar hypoplasia.

records.label: Child with SSMD (family 1)
records.segregation: c.587+5G>A inherited from mother; c.588-8_588-4del de novo; parents unaffected
quotes: Whole exome sequencing of a child affected with SSMD and her unaffected parents identified two rare variants in GPX4. The first (c.587+5G>A) was inherited from the mother, and the second (c.588-8_588-4del) was de novo (NM_001039848.1); both were predicted to impact splicing of GPX4.
records.genotype_reason: two different heterozygous variants in one gene

records.label: Second child with SSMD (family 2)
records.segregation: Both unaffected parents heterozygous for c.381C>A; child's DNA not available
quotes: Subsequently, a second child with SSMD was identified; although DNA from the child was not available, the two unaffected parents were found by Sanger sequencing to each carry the same heterozygous stop mutation in exon 3 of GPX4, c.381C>A, p.Tyr127* (NM_001039848.1).

notes.statement: Smith et al. (2014) described Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia as a neonatal lethal form of SMD characterized by severe metaphyseal chondrodysplasia with mild limb shortening, platyspondyly, cardiac conduction defects, and central nervous system abnormalities.
quotes: Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia (SSMD) is a neonatal lethal form of spondylometaphyseal dysplasia characterised by severe metaphyseal chondrodysplasia with mild limb shortening, platyspondyly, cardiac conduction defects, and central nervous system abnormalities.

notes.statement: Smith et al. (2014) showed by in vitro studies that the two GPX4 splice mutations in an SSMD patient spliced out part of exon 4 and caused skipping of exon 5, respectively, both resulting in frameshift and premature truncation of GPX4.
quotes: In vitro studies confirmed the mutations spliced out part of exon 4 and skipped exon 5, respectively, with both resulting in a frameshift and premature truncation of GPX4.

notes.statement: Aygun et al. (2012) suggested that central nervous system malformations might be a major component of Sedaghatian type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia and should be evaluated in detail to possibly uncover the underlying pathophysiology.
quotes: central nervous system malformations might be a major component of the disorder and should be evaluated in detail to possibly uncover the underlying pathophysiology

notes.statement: English et al. (2006) suggested that Sedaghatian spondylometaphyseal dysplasia may be associated with neuronal migration abnormalities and proposed a novel association with agenesis of the corpus callosum.
quotes: Our case highlights the possibility for neuronal migration abnormalities in Sedaghatian spondylometaphyseal dysplasia and suggests a novel association of the disorder with agenesis of the corpus callosum.

notes.statement: Koutouby et al. (2000) reported an infant with Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia who survived 161 days, whereas all previously reported cases had died within 4 days of life. Extensive investigations were performed, and genomic DNA analysis of the patient and parents did not identify an abnormal gene.
quotes: Although all previously reported cases died within 4 days of life, our patient survived 161 days.
Genomic DNA analysis of patient and parents were sent to the Faculty de Medicine Xavier Bichat, France, but yet abnormal gene could not be detected.

notes.statement: Elçioglu and Hall (1998) described the radiological findings in 2 unrelated patients with Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia and, after reviewing the literature, identified additional anomalies including disproportionately long fibulae, dysharmonious maturation, and turricephaly.
quotes: We review the literature and identify additional anomalies including disproportionately long fibulae, dysharmonious maturation and turricephaly.

notes.statement: Sedaghatian (1980) suggested that the disorder is an autosomal recessive trait, because the parents of the 2 affected brothers were normal and later had an affected daughter.
quotes: since parents are normal and recently had an affected baby girl, it is presumed that this disorder is an autosomal recessive trait.

notes.statement: Sedaghatian (1980) attributed the low calcium, high phosphorus and high alkaline phosphatase in one affected infant to a renal defect. The author stated that how these findings relate to the skeletal and cardiac abnormalities was unclear.
quotes: low calcium, high phosphorus, and high alkaline phosphatase levels attributed to a renal defect
The pathogenetic relationship between these manifestations is presently unclear

notes.statement: Opitz et al. (1987) suggested that Sedaghatian syndrome is an autosomal recessive trait with high gene frequency in Iranians, based on the occurrence of affected children of both sexes born to normal first-cousin parents and the apparent confinement of the disorder to Iranians.
quotes: The occurrence in children of both sexes in one instance, born to normal parents who were first cousins, and currently apparent confinement of the disorder to Iranians suggests that the Sedaghatian syndrome is an autosomal recessive trait with high gene frequency in Iranians.

notes.statement: Opitz et al. (1987) suggested that Sedaghatian syndrome may be a more complexly pleiotropic syndrome than the radiographs indicate, since one of Sedaghatian's original patients also had microphthalmia, ear asymmetry, depressed nasal bridge, broad nose, short neck, prominent sternum, and short lower extremities.
quotes: This may be a more complexly pleiotropic syndrome than suggested by the roentgenograms, since one of Sedaghatian's patients also had "microphthalmia, asymmetry of ears, depressed nasal bridge, broad nose, short neck, prominent sternum, and short lower extremities."

notes.statement: Peeden et al. (1992) noted that an earlier-reported Iranian infant with a similar perinatal course and similar radiographs was born to first-cousin parents, which suggested an autosomal recessive single-gene defect.
quotes: This infant was born to first cousins, suggesting an autosomal recessive single gene defect.
